title: HAVING a Bad Day
subtitle: Fix the broken query that's supposed to catch cheaters
conceptSummary: HAVING filters GROUPS (after GROUP BY). WHERE filters ROWS (before grouping). They're not interchangeable!

dialogue.text: I tried to find all players with total runs over 100, but my query crashed! It says WHERE can't use aggregate functions.
Because WHERE runs BEFORE grouping. You need HAVING — it filters AFTER the group is computed.

teachMoment.title: HAVING vs WHERE
teachMoment.body:
ORDER OF OPERATIONS:
1. FROM (get the table)
2. WHERE (filter rows)
3. GROUP BY (group them)
4. HAVING (filter groups)
5. SELECT (pick columns)
6. ORDER BY (sort)
7. LIMIT (cut)

❌ WHERE SUM(runs_scored) > 100 — WRONG
✅ HAVING SUM(runs_scored) > 100 — CORRECT

task.instruction: Fix Byte's broken query. It should find all players with total runs OVER 100.
task.brokenQuery:
SELECT player_id, SUM(runs_scored) AS total_runs
FROM match_stats
GROUP BY player_id
WHERE SUM(runs_scored) > 100
task.solution: SELECT player_id, SUM(runs_scored) AS total_runs FROM match_stats GROUP BY player_id HAVING SUM(runs_scored) > 100
task.errorInQuery: WHERE used instead of HAVING for aggregate filter

hints.text: The issue is WHERE is in the wrong place. It can't filter aggregated values.
Replace WHERE with HAVING. HAVING goes AFTER GROUP BY.
Fix: change WHERE to HAVING, keeping it after GROUP BY: HAVING SUM(runs_scored) > 100

winDialogue.text: Player 1 is the only one over 100 total runs. Conclusive proof of stat manipulation!
Good work. Now we need to find DISTINCT players and discount codes involved. No duplicates.

storyBeat: The data clearly shows stat manipulation targeting Player 1. But who entered these records? We need to find all unique discount codes and user IDs from the logs.
